title: Operadic correspondences and their left Kan extensions
statement:
Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads and algebras of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and coherent diagrams and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Relative limit cones and joins have the meaning of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $S$ be a small quasicategory. An $S$-family of generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads is a categorical fibration $\pi:\mathcal M\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times S$ satisfying the following conditions. Here categorical fibration means an inner fibration which lifts equivalences with prescribed source. For each $s\in S$, its fiber $\mathcal M_s\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad; every inert base arrow has a cocartesian lift for the projection $\mathcal M_s\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ within this fiber. These lifts give relative $\pi$-limit Segal cones: for $x$ over $([r],s)$, take the inert restrictions to its $r$ consecutive edges $[1]$ and its $r+1$ vertices $[0]$, together with the endpoint arrows from each edge to its two vertices; the cone from $x$ to this incidence diagram is a $\pi$-limit. For $r=0$ this diagram consists of the single vertex $[0]$. A map from such a family to a monoidal infinity category $\mathcal V^\otimes$ of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category] is a functor over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserving these fiberwise inert edges. Let $\mathcal E_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathcal M,\mathcal V^\otimes)$ on those functors, with coherent transformations over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$.

A correspondence is an $S$-family for $S=\Delta^1$; put $\mathcal A=\mathcal M_0$ and $\mathcal B=\mathcal M_1$. It is constant over $[0]$ if $\mathcal M_{[0]}\to\Delta^1$ is a cocartesian fibration classified by an equivalence $\mathcal A_{[0]}\simeq\mathcal B_{[0]}$. Only correspondences with both these fibers spaces are considered below. An edge is active if its image in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is opposite to a map preserving endpoints. For $b\in\mathcal B_{[1]}$ set $J_b=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{act}})_{/b}$.

For an active diagram $T:K\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ and an active cocone $T\to v$ with $v\in\mathcal V$, call the cocone weakly operadically colimiting if restriction gives an equivalence from active arrows $v\to w$ to coherent active cocones $T\to w$ for every $w\in\mathcal V$. It is operadically colimiting if both $L\oplus T\to L\oplus v$ and $T\oplus R\to v\oplus R$ are weakly operadically colimiting for every finite tuple $L$ or $R$, including the empty tuple. Here weakly operadically colimiting for a tuple apex uses active arrows from that tuple to $w$; $\oplus$ is concatenation under the monoidal Segal identifications, including the empty tuple. An inert-preserving functor $H:\mathcal M\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an operadic left Kan extension of $H|_{\mathcal A}$ if, for every color $b$ of $\mathcal B$, its induced cocone $J_b\to H(b)$ is operadically colimiting. These are the mapping-space forms of the operadic cocone definitions; no existence of colimits or extensions is included in this definition.
